brief.situation: You are the night security operations lead at Harbor Point, a fictional colocation data center. At 01:00 the access system reports a tailgate at data hall mantrap B: one contractor's badge, two people through. Two guards are on site, plus two night technicians in the data hall. Facilities systems report to your console too.
handover: You can dispatch the guards, change door modes, start standby plant from the building management system, call out the on-call engineer and call the police. Guards observe and escort; they are not to confront alone.
Data hall cooling is N+1: CRAC-1 and CRAC-2 run, CRAC-3 is standby.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock.
Alarms, zones, cameras (described in words), the environment and the door log update as events happen.
When you close the incident you write the report and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Fifteen minutes for the unbadged person to reach cage C7 is the author's figure.

writeup.question: For the incident report: what happened at the door and why, how you protected people and the customer, how you handled the cooling failure, and what should change.

parts.label: The tailgate
parts.criteria: Recognizes tailgating via social engineering (one badge, two people; the contractor held the door for a claimed colleague); verified on camera and the visitor log; intercepted with two guards observing and escorting rather than one guard confronting; police for the trespasser; the contractor's badge suspended pending review.
parts.modelAnswer: Okoye held the mantrap door for a man claiming to be with the carrier: a tailgate through social engineering. Camera and visitor log confirmed he had no access. Two guards escorted him to the desk; police called; Okoye's badge suspended.

parts.label: People and the customer
parts.criteria: Entry restricted while exit stays free (life safety: never lock egress); the customer notified of the approach to their cage; evidence exported with custody.
parts.modelAnswer: I suspended badge-in but kept exit free, because egress doors must always open. The customer was told; the clips and badge log were exported, hashed and logged.

parts.label: Cooling and lessons
parts.criteria: Started the N+1 standby unit at once and called the engineer for the breaker; did not prop doors (defeats access control); kept inlet temperature within or near the recommended range; changes: tailgate training, mantrap anti-passback, alarms on held doors.
parts.modelAnswer: I started CRAC-3 from the BMS within minutes and called out the engineer; temperatures stayed under 27 °C. Changes: contractor briefing on tailgating, mantrap occupancy enforcement, review of cage latch alarms.

expertPath.text: Dispatch both guards together; review mantrap B and the visitor log; suspend badge-in (exit stays free).
Call Okoye; suspend his badge pending review; the guards hold the man at the desk; call the police.
Breaker trip: start CRAC-3 from the BMS; call out the engineer.
Export the clips and badge log with custody; a full report.

handled.headline: Good: people, access, cooling, evidence
handled.body: Two guards escorted him before he reached a cage, entry was restricted without locking anyone in, the standby unit held the temperature, and the evidence is kept.

handledGaps.headline: Handled, with gaps
handledGaps.body: Speed matters at a tailgate; egress stays free; standby cooling first, the engineer second; preserve the clips and log before they roll over.

peopleHarm.headline: Life safety comes first
peopleHarm.body: Egress doors must always open, and a guard should never confront an intruder alone. Security controls that endanger people are the wrong controls.

breach.headline: Too slow at the door
breach.body: A tailgate is an intrusion until proven otherwise: dispatch at once, verify in parallel.

hallHot.headline: Cooling lost
hallHot.body: With N+1 cooling, the standby unit is minutes away from the BMS; waiting for the engineer let the hall pass the allowable limit.

time_up.headline: No report
time_up.body: The shift ran out without a report.

scoring.modelReasoning: Tailgate through social engineering: two guards escort, police, the contractor's badge suspended; entry suspended with free exit; customer told; evidence with custody. Cooling: CRAC-3 from the BMS at once, engineer called; no propped doors; inlet under 27 °C. Lessons: contractor training, mantrap enforcement, held-door alarms.
